codeReview.summary: The shared truncate helper was added and three UI call sites now import it, but the feature does not fully satisfy the consolidation contract because the commit also changed browser-read-tools semantics and left other duplicate truncation helpers in the extension unchanged.

issues.description: The local helper still duplicates truncation behavior instead of importing the shared utility, so the implementation does not achieve the promised 'single truncate implementation' / 'all 6 locations import from shared' outcome required by the feature description and VAL-CON-004.

The refactor changed behavior: untruncated results are now always copied via `slice(0, limit)` and the helper no longer returns the original string reference on short inputs. This is a runtime change in a read-only consolidation task, contrary to mission guidance to preserve behavior while refactoring.

A duplicate truncation implementation remains (`slice(0, 57) + '...'`) even though the feature claims all six truncate() duplicates were consolidated. Leaving this call site unchanged means the repository still contains additional ad hoc truncation logic after the feature completed.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The `refactor-worker` skill still frames repo-standards as a mandatory final validation gate, but this mission repeatedly hit pre-existing unrelated failures and workers documented them instead. The skill should explicitly describe how to handle diff-scoped or pre-existing repo-standards failures during focused cleanup work.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: .factory/skills/refactor-worker/SKILL.md final validation step vs handoff skillFeedback for consolidate-truncate (`followedProcedure: false` because `npm run check:repo-standards` failed on unrelated files).

sharedStateObservations.observation: The mission guidance says consolidation should create shared utilities in `@parchi/shared`, but there is no explicit convention for when similar truncation helpers that return metadata objects must wrap the shared helper versus remaining local. This ambiguity likely contributed to `browser-read-tools.ts` keeping an inline truncation helper while the feature still claimed full consolidation.

summary: Review failed: commit 938f99f adds a shared truncate helper, but it does not complete the promised consolidation. `browser-read-tools.ts` still contains a local truncate implementation and the commit also changes that helper's behavior, while other duplicate truncation logic remains elsewhere in the extension.
